title: Per-phoneme d_nominal / d_floor, ARPAbet
spec_reference: Section 7 (d(c) = max(d_floor(c), d_nominal(c) * rho^gamma)); Section 17 F4; Section 22 failure #10
blocked_reason: Awaiting the exact numeric transcription of Klatt (1979) Table 1. The source is decided; only the numbers are missing. Klatt 1979 and Festival are both unreachable from this environment - every document host returns HTTP 403 at CONNECT under organization egress policy - so the values must be supplied. NOTHING has been populated from memory, inference, Festival, or secondary literature.
required_source_material: AUTHORITATIVE: Klatt, D. H. (1979). Synthesis by Rule of Segmental Durations in English Sentences. Table 1. INHDUR -> d_nominal_s, MINDUR -> d_floor_s.
DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, never imported: Festival lib/klatt_durs.scm / Allen, Hunnicutt & Klatt (1987) ch. 9.

sourcing_findings.note: Established from bibliographic search only. No duration value was obtained; these are findings about WHERE the two columns live, so the extraction task is unambiguous.
sourcing_findings.d_floor_may_not_be_in_the_named_sources: SUPERSEDED by source_authority_decision. Retained for history: d_floor is an incompressible floor corresponding to Klatt's MINDUR, which appears with INHDUR in DUR = MINDUR + (INHDUR - MINDUR) * PRCNT/100. The spec owner has since designated Klatt (1979) Table 1 as the authoritative source for BOTH columns, and Festival / Allen, Hunnicutt & Klatt (1987) as diagnostic only.
sourcing_findings.dialect: The lexicon is CMUdict (US English, Section 9). Duration values must be for American English. Crystal & House (1988) is American English. Confirm the dialect of any substitute source.

acceptance_requirements: All 24 ARPAbet consonants covered: B CH D DH F G HH JH K L M N NG P R S SH T TH V W Y Z ZH.
Every Klatt symbol mapped to ARPAbet, with the mapping recorded per row.
BOTH INHDUR and MINDUR present for all 24. A row missing either is an error, not a gap.
MINDUR <= INHDUR for every consonant (d_floor_s <= d_nominal_s).
Every entry carries 'source' and 'page_or_table' naming Klatt (1979) Table 1.
No interpolation, no estimation by manner class, no defaults, no Festival values.
Partial coverage leaves F4 UNPOPULATED and is reported as an explicit gap list.

source_authority_decision.decided_by: spec owner, [CHATGPT HANDOFF - F4 source authority decision]
source_authority_decision.authoritative_source: Klatt, D. H. (1979). Synthesis by Rule of Segmental Durations in English Sentences. Table 1.

table_1_defines.INHDUR: inherent duration of a segment, in milliseconds

source_authority_decision.d_floor_caveat: MINDUR is a MODEL-DERIVED LOWER BOUND, not a physiological minimum. Section 7 already forbids describing the compression equation as validated science; d_floor inherits the same caveat and no output may claim otherwise.
source_authority_decision.festival_allen_1987: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Festival lib/klatt_durs.scm, tied to Allen, Hunnicutt & Klatt (1987) chapter 9, contains values that differ from Klatt 1979 and therefore represents a later source/version. It must NEVER be imported, averaged, merged into, or substituted for F4.
source_authority_decision.supersedes: An earlier note in this fixture suggested the MITalk table might be the cleanest single source for both columns. That was a sourcing observation, not a decision, and it is now SUPERSEDED: Klatt 1979 Table 1 is authoritative for both columns.
